When the session ends, a StopTransactionReq OCPP message is sent to the OCPP server, followed by a StatusNotificationReq with an “Available” status. This informs the OCPP server and the SCM that the charger is now free and ready to serve other vehicles. 5.2 CHIL/PHIL Verification Testing The final verification of system performance requires the SCM to manage all charging and DER as emulated and represented in the CHIL/PHIL test bed above. Unlike the simulation results above, this verification step ensures real-time operation with real-world communication protocols. CHIL testing ensures the system will perform at scale, while PHIL testing ensures the SCM can respond to live operating EVSE hardware. The results below, when compared to simulation results, provide the confidence this technology is ready for deployment in pilot demonstrations. 5.2.1 CHIL/PHIL Test Results: Gold SCM A 24-hour demonstration test was conducted with the CHIL/PHIL environment from about 12 p.m. on Oct. 28 to 12 p.m. on Oct. 29, 2025. The test start time of 12 p.m. was converted internally to an emulation time starting at 6 a.m. in order to synchronize different load profiles (such as EV arrival patterns, solar generation, and building demand) and standardize the results. The test setup included the Gold SCM control framework, 294 EV arrivals scheduled throughout the day (sampled from the full approximately 1,000 EV daily arrivals predicted by the EVI- Rental model), and two hardware-based EV-EVSE sessions.
